from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeRegressor

# max_depth and min_samples_leaf are the primary
# overfitting controls on noisy financial data
tree_model = DecisionTreeRegressor(
    max_depth=4,
    min_samples_leaf=50,
    random_state=0
)
tree_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
caption: An unconstrained tree can memorize noise -- max_depth and min_samples_leaf keep it honest.

eyebrow: A first look at what matters
code:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
import pandas as pd

forest_model = RandomForestRegressor(
    n_estimators=300, max_depth=6,
    min_samples_leaf=30, max_features="sqrt",
    random_state=0, n_jobs=-1
)
forest_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
importances = pd.Series(forest_model.feature_importances_,
                         index=X_train.columns)
print(importances.sort_values(ascending=False).head(10))
caption: feature_importances_ gives a rough first look -- Chapter 5 covers more robust alternatives.
